title: Cybersecurity AI startup Corma reaches $1B valuation in about 3 months
slides: Can a 3-month-old startup really be worth $1B?
Corma hit that valuation faster than almost any security firm
Its edge: AI that maps attacker behavior, not just signatures
Security teams may soon face pressure to adopt or fall behind
Ask your vendor one question: what does your AI actually catch?
thread_text:
1. $1B in 90 days?

Corma just hit unicorn status faster than almost any security firm in history. The money isn't betting on malware signatures—it's betting on a completely different way of seeing attacks.

2. The real edge

Corma's AI doesn't just match known threats. It maps how attackers actually behave—movement patterns, not fingerprints. That means it can catch what signatures miss entirely.

3. Pressure is coming

If this works at scale, security teams will face a simple choice: adopt behavior-based AI or fall behind attackers who already have it. The gap won't close on its own.

4. One question to ask

When your vendor pitches AI, don't ask if they have it. Ask what it actually catches that your current stack doesn't. Most can't answer specifically.

5. Test it now

Pick one recent alert your team missed. Ask your vendor to show how their AI would have caught it. If they can't walk through the behavior, you have your answer.
